input.question: Can a piece of toilet paper absorb the same amount of water after a cycle of wet-dry-wet?
input.ground_truth: Probably not. Toilet paper is designed to break up in water. I would expect the gaps in the fibers, the gaps that hold the water, would collapse as it soaks, leaving less volume for water retention after drying out.

response.prediction: After a cycle of wetting and drying, a piece of toilet paper may not be able to absorb as much water as it did the first time. When toilet paper gets wet and then dries, it can become less absorbent because the fibers may swell and then harden. This means that after the wet-dry cycle, the toilet paper’s ability to soak up more water is reduced. So, it usually cannot absorb the same amount of water again after being wet and dried.
